⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's check the rest for Case 2 (D=E=3, B=2)." end="All constraints satisfied. The solution is valid." basis=The solver explores an alternative coloring (Case 2), verifies it is valid, but then returns to the first solution (Sol 1) to present it.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=probable start="Let's check if I can pick I=3." end="So C=2 is fine." basis=The solver explores assigning 3 to I, verifies it works, but later discards it in favor of Blue.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Wait, I need to check if F is connected to B in my thought process?" end="Is F connected to A? No." basis=The solver re-reads the edge list and re-verifies F's connections verbatim, having just done so a few paragraphs prior.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="I will write down the reasoning clearly." end="This matches my previous derivation. The logic holds up." basis=The solver re-executes the entire step-by-step coloring process from scratch in a summary format, after having already derived and verified the solution multiple times.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=probable start="Let's start with A. A = Red (R)." end="These must be Blue (B) or Green (G)." basis=The solver restarts the coloring process from A, re-executing the assignment of A and its neighbors which was just attempted before a digression about known graphs.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Wait, I assigned E=G and F=G. Are E and F connected?" end="Let's re-verify the previous solution F=R just to be sure." basis=The solver explores assigning Green to F, verifies it is valid, but then returns to the previous solution where F is Red.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="What if I swap Red and Blue?" end="Let's pick one to present. The first one is fine." basis=The solver explores swapping Red and Blue colors, finds a valid alternative, but discards it in favor of the first solution.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Let's try to assign in this order." end="Yes, it is the same solution!" basis=The solver re-executes the coloring process step-by-step in the audit order to verify consistency, ending up with the exact same solution and adding no new information.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="Let's try a systematic backtracking assignment." end="Neighbors of A (B, D, E, G, I) cannot be R." basis=The solver restarts the coloring process with a systematic approach, re-executing the assignment of A and its neighbors which was just done in the preliminary analysis.
